source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which pill is preferred for a breastfeeding mother at 6 weeks postpartum?
questions.rationale: POPs (lynestrenol, desogestrel) can be used from 6 weeks postpartum without affecting milk quantity or quality.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 Progestin-only pills (PDF p. 84)
questions.quote: Can be used by breastfeeding mothers six weeks after childbirth without affecting the quality and quantity of breast milk

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: What is the main way progestin-only pills prevent pregnancy?
questions.rationale: POPs mainly thicken cervical mucus (effective after 48 hours) and suppress ovulation in some cycles.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 How POPs work (PDF p. 83)
questions.quote: POPs mainly thicken the cervical mucus and impair the entry of sperm into the uterus.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A non-breastfeeding woman on lynestrenol POP took her pill 5 hours late. She should:
questions.rationale: Lynestrenol POP more than 3 hours late (desogestrel >12 hours): resume and use backup or abstain for 48 hours.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 Missed POPs (PDF p. 91)
questions.quote: during the first 48 hours after restarting the pills

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which statement about progestin-only pills is correct?
questions.rationale: POPs are taken one daily at the same time, starting a new pack the day after finishing.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 Taking the POP (PDF p. 91)
questions.quote: take one pill every day at the same time until the packet is finished

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A POP user has had no menses for 50 days. The nurse advises:
questions.rationale: No menses for more than 45 days on POPs warrants examination and a pregnancy test.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 Missed POPs (PDF p. 92)
questions.quote: If she fails to have her menses for more than 45 days, she should see her healthcare provider

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: The only MEC Category 4 condition for progestin-only pills is:
questions.rationale: Current breast cancer is the only Category 4 condition for POPs.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 MEC for POPs (PDF p. 87)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: How often is DMPA 150 mg given?
questions.rationale: DMPA every 12 weeks (3 months); NET-EN every 8 weeks.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 POI administration (PDF p. 100)
questions.quote: One dose of DMPA (150 mg) by deep IM injection given every 12 weeks

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: After giving DMPA, the nurse tells the client not to massage the site because massage:
questions.rationale: Massaging the site makes DMPA absorb too fast.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 DMPA administration (PDF p. 101)
questions.quote: Instruct the client not to massage or rub the site, as this can cause the DMPA to be absorbed fast.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Why is the DMPA vial gently shaken before drawing the dose?
questions.rationale: Without mixing, drug remains as sediment, giving an inadequate dose; vigorous shaking makes it foamy.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 DMPA administration (PDF p. 100)
questions.quote: Failure to mix the solution will cause some of the drug to remain as sediment in the vial

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A DMPA client returns 3 weeks after her due date. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: DMPA can be given up to 4 weeks late without backup or pregnancy assessment.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 POI follow-up (PDF p. 103)
questions.quote: If the client is less than four weeks late for the next DMPA

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which side effect is most common after a year of DMPA use?
questions.rationale: About half of DMPA users have amenorrhea after a year; it is harmful to neither health nor future fertility.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 POI effects (PDF p. 104)
questions.quote: Another 50% of women using DMPA develop amenorrhea after a year of use.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A woman plans to conceive within 6 months. Why might DMPA be a poor choice?
questions.rationale: Return of fertility is delayed by an average of 9–10 months after the last DMPA injection, but it is not permanent.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 Stopping POIs (PDF p. 105)
questions.quote: The average delay in return of fertility is 9 to 10 months for DMPA

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A DMPA user worries that her lack of menses means blood is 'building up' inside. The nurse explains:
options: It is not harmful or retained
questions.rationale: Amenorrhea is an expected effect on the endometrium; blood is not building up and it does not mean pregnancy.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 POI effects (PDF p. 104)
questions.quote: menstrual blood is not building up inside her

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which advice helps a DMPA user manage weight gain?
questions.rationale: Weight gain of about 1–2 kg per year from increased appetite can be controlled with a low-calorie diet.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 POI effects (PDF p. 104)
questions.quote: can be controlled by shifting to a low-calorie diet

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Implanon (single-rod etonogestrel implant) provides protection for:
questions.rationale: Implanon lasts 3 years; Jadelle (two rods, levonorgestrel) lasts up to 5 years.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 Subdermal implants (PDF p. 107)
questions.quote: The single-rod system (Implanon) releases etonogestrel and has a life span of three years.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Where is a subdermal contraceptive implant inserted?
questions.rationale: Implants go under the skin of the inner upper arm, 8–10 cm from the medial epicondyle, under local anesthesia.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 Implant insertion (PDF p. 112)
questions.quote: Mark the insertion site (8 cm to 10 cm from the medial epicondyle).

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which is an advantage of subdermal implants?
questions.rationale: Fertility returns almost immediately after removal; insertion and removal need a trained provider.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 Implant advantages (PDF p. 107)
questions.quote: Reversible, as fertility returns almost immediately after the rods are removed

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A client asks whether progestin injectables cause abortion. The nurse answers that POIs:
questions.rationale: POIs neither disrupt an existing pregnancy nor cause abortion or birth defects; fertility returns after a delay.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 Facts about POIs (PDF p. 106)
questions.quote: POIs neither disrupt an existing pregnancy nor cause an abortion.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A woman on DMPA bleeds lightly but irregularly. When is her next injection due?
questions.rationale: Bleeding should not guide the schedule; DMPA is given every 3 months regardless of bleeding.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 5 Facts about POIs (PDF p. 106)
questions.quote: bleeding episodes should not be used as a guide for the injection schedule
